text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Algirdas Brazauskas said in Madrid that Lithuania expects to get into the second round of NATO expansion in 1999.
- The Lithuanian government decided to include Mazeikiu Nafta in the list of key enterprises to be privatised by international tenders.
- Siauliu Bank posted a 1.01 million litas net profit for the first half of 1997.
- Lithuanian Gas bought and transported 1.368 billion cubic metres of natural gas in the first six months of this year, 2.5 percent more than the same period in 1996.
- The chairman of Lithuanian Savings Bank Romualdas Visokavichius has little doubt that the state-run bank will be slated for privatisation in a year or two.
- Lithuanian politicians cautiously welcomed the decision to inlcude Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic in the first of NATO expansion and to leave the door open to the Baltic countries.
- Hermis Bank posted a 14.3 million litas net profit for the first half of 1997.

- The Lithuanian statistics department said that 18 percent of the country's population lived under the poverty line in 1996. In the big cities 12 percent of the population lived in poverty while the rate in rural areas was 26 percent.
